# Project Ops
Project Ops is the `@missher/dsh-project-ops` plugin for DeepSeek Harness. It puts one entry in the
session header: browse the files this conversation registered next to the project's development plan
s, open a file in the Host's native right-sidebar preview, or reveal it in Finder and hand the actua
l file to someone by copy or drag-and-drop.
Desktop app · Install · Task documents
## Current state

- Current version: **1.0.3**. Download the matching package and checksum from the v1.0.3 Release.
-
Built for the DeepSeek Harness 0.2 series; compatibility is probed through the methods the plugin ac

tually calls, not pinned to one exact Host version.
- A package existing, the source being upgraded
and a profile having loaded the plugin are three different states; trust the source you installed an
d what the Host actually loaded.
## What you get
- **Session files**: the files this conversation registered — native `present` deliveries plus succe
ssful `write`, `edit` and `str_replace_editor` changes. The list comes from session history and may

keep entries later moved or deleted; text listed in an `artifacts[]` report is not a file record.
-
**Categories**: All, Plans, Word, Excel, PPT, PDF, Images, Media, Other, chosen by real extension; `

plan.docx` is a Word file, never a development plan.
- **Native preview**: clicking a file name open
s the Host's own right-sidebar file preview; whether content is rendered depends on the Host's suppo

rt for that format.
- **Show in folder**: reveals and selects the file in Finder so you can copy the

file itself or drag it into a chat window — not just copy its path.
- **Development plans**: the sa
me panel lists this project's `docs/tasks` tasks and their "Plan / Delivery record" document entries
e panel lists this project's `docs/tasks` tasks and their "Plan / Delivery record" document entries.
## Use it

1. Install the plugin into the target profile (see Install).
2. Open a session and click **Project O

ps** in the session header.
3. Filter by category; click a **file name** to open the native preview.
4. Click **Show in folder** on the same row: Finder opens with the file selected; copy or drag it f

rom there.
5. Switch to the Plans area to open PLAN / delivery records. `Escape` closes the panel; `
Tab` moves inside it.
## Categories and file sources
Categories are derived from the extension only, never from words such as "plan" in a name:
| Category | Extensions |

| Word | doc, docx, docm, odt, rtf |
| Excel | xls, xlsx, xlsm, xlsb, ods, csv, tsv |
| PPT | ppt, p

ptx, pptm, odp |
| PDF | pdf |
| Images | png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, svg, avif, bmp, tif, tiff |
| M

edia | mp3, wav, m4a, flac, ogg, mp4, mov, webm, mkv, avi |
| Other | everything else, including sou

a, flac, ogg, mp4, mov, webm, mkv, avi |
| Other | everything else, including source code and text |
- One absolute path keeps only its latest record; identical file names in different directories stay

separate and gain an extra directory line when a name would otherwise be ambiguous.
- The list foll
ows the session's file records and is restored from Host history after a reload; at most the latest

1000 distinct paths are kept, and the limit is reported.
- "File index unavailable" and "no files" a
re different states with different copy; a missing capability is never rendered as an empty list.
## Search history
A short **Search** tab records this session's native search output; it is separate from delivered fi
les and never adds a delivery:
- Sources: `glob` `meta.paths`, `grep` `meta.files[].path`, `web_search` `meta.sources[]` (title + h
ttp(s) URL), a successful `web_fetch` (`meta.url` with a 2xx `statusCode`) under **Opened pages**, a

nd the `query` argument of `session_search`/`session_event_search`.
- Only structured metadata is st
ored — never grep hit lines, snippets or page bodies — and free text is never parsed back into paths

.
- Local hits open the native preview and **Show in folder**; web sources are plain http(s) links.
Hits are deduplicated within one call, and relative hits resolve against the tool's `working-directo
ry/change`; a relative hit without a known absolute working directory is omitted instead of becoming

a wrong clickable path.
- A failed call is shown as a failure and never contributes hits. Zero-hit
searches are kept; Host truncation (`truncated`/`total`) and this plugin's own caps (50 searches, 10

0 paths and 50 sources per search) are reported as incomplete.
- History is per session. An older Ho
st without the projection shows "search history unavailable", and replay fills only the native event
s the Host still retains (checkpoint/window) — it never re-runs a search. Session queries have no st
ructured result metadata on this Host, so only their query is recorded ("results in the session"); t
heir results are never parsed or copied.
## Plans and delivery records
- For a development task of real size the agent maintains `docs/tasks/<date>-<slug>-<identity>/PLAN.
md`, continues it as work progresses and writes `READY.md` after the delivery review. Ordinary quest

ions and tiny edits do not require one.
- Task rows carry four short states: delivery linked to the
current plan, plan updated, record needs review, plan in progress. **"Delivery linked to the current
plan" only means the record matches the current plan revision; it is not an acceptance, a release o

r an install.**
- Document entries open the native preview; missing documents stay visible but disab
led with the reason in the tooltip. Opening one from the Plans area closes the panel.
## Preview, show in folder and missing files
- Clicking a file name asks the Host filesystem whether the path is still accessible before opening
the native preview; a moved, deleted or unreadable file shows an inline error. Whether the file rend

ers is up to the Host's support for its format, so not every file is guaranteed a content preview.
-
"Show in folder" calls the Host's native session file-location action (`session/openWorkspacePath`
with `reveal`). On macOS the Host runs `open -R`, which selects the file in Finder. The plugin never

builds shell strings and never starts a service.
